pitchSummary: CivicState sells citation-backed constituent letters, but remains watchlist until demand and safety validate.

authority.note: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

methods: Read available root docs and planning artifacts.
Inspected package metadata, Prisma schema, API routes, worker agents, and compliance/payment/delivery code.
Tagged repo facts as evidence and external market statements as assumptions.

thesis.current: CivicState is a narrow transactional civic correspondence tool: research, draft, charge, deliver, and track constituent letters.
thesis.reason: Repo has product implementation, but no workspace evidence of paid demand, production deliverability, official coverage, or legal/compliance clearance.

registryContext.sensitivity: Watchlist; personal/research asset; not near-term investible unless operator confirms business intent.
registryContext.identityMismatch: Dispatch says brooks-history / RPLogic-Inc/brookss-history; repo content says CivicState.

customer.primary: Individual US residents with a specific civic concern and need for professional official correspondence. [assumption: inferred from repo docs]
excluded: Legal claimants or people seeking legal advice. [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
Businesses seeking lobbying or government affairs services. [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md]
Organizations needing enterprise advocacy tooling. [assumption: not in launch scope]

realToday: Submission API with moderation and queueing. [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/submissions.ts]
AI researcher and drafter agents with citation constraints. [evidence: apps/worker/src/agents/researcher.ts; apps/worker/src/agents/drafter.ts]
Postmark delivery and webhooks. [evidence: apps/worker/src/agents/delivery.ts; apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts]
Dashboard, admin, and compliance surfaces. [evidence: apps/web and apps/api route files]
notYetProven: Production conversion. [assumption: no revenue evidence found]
Production deliverability. [assumption: no Postmark metrics found]
Legal/compliance sufficiency. [assumption: no legal review evidence found]

model: 10 issue clusters per unit per year. [assumption: operator planning heuristic]
20 trigger events per cluster per year. [assumption: civic event heuristic]
20 paid campaigns per trigger event. [assumption: small adoption hypothesis]
$15 blended campaign price. [assumption: midpoint of repo pricing tiers]
$3,060,000 annual launchable revenue. [assumption: 51 x 10 x 20 x 20 x $15]
marketSizing.caution: This is a validation hypothesis, not evidence of market demand.

missing: Legal review cost. [assumption: absent from repo]
Data-provider cost beyond planning notes. [assumption: absent from repo]
Refunds and chargebacks. [assumption: absent from repo]

competition: Resistbot [assumption: model knowledge, not workspace evidence]
Change.org [assumption: model knowledge, not workspace evidence]
Quorum/FiscalNote-style enterprise advocacy tools [assumption: model knowledge, not workspace evidence]
VoterVoice/Phone2Action-style grassroots advocacy tools [assumption: model knowledge, not workspace evidence]
Manual email and phone calls [evidence: substitute implied by repo value proposition]
Lawyers and legal document services [evidence: repo explicitly excludes legal advice]

goToMarket.firstMotion: Manual beta plus issue-specific landing/workflow pages. [assumption: EIR strategy]
metrics: 25 recruited beta users. [assumption: manual validation target]
10 real paid beta campaigns. [assumption: minimum willingness-to-pay signal]
Delivery, bounce, spam complaint, refund, and support rates. [assumption: key risk metrics]

killCase: This may be a personal/research asset, not a company. [evidence: registry note]
Repo/project identity mismatch undermines data-room credibility. [evidence: worker dispatch; package.json]
Official deliverability may fail. [assumption: product mechanics]
Legal/compliance exposure may exceed the value of low-priced campaigns. [assumption: risk analysis]
Willingness to pay may be too low for a repeatable business. [assumption: no traction evidence]
Compliance implementation has apparent schema mismatches. [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/compliance.ts; packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma]
doNotDo: Do not pitch as VC-ready before paid conversion and deliverability evidence.
Do not add automated follow-up letters before legal/compliance review.
Do not add organizational APIs before consumer workflow validation.
Do not represent citation-backed letters as legal advice.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay $5-$25 for one civic letter campaign.
assumptionLedger.basis: Repo pricing exists; no traction evidence.
assumptionLedger.validation: Run beta checkout and record conversion/refunds.
Track tier mix across first 100 paid campaigns. [assumption: validation sample target]

assumptionLedger.assumption: Official email delivery can work at acceptable rates.
assumptionLedger.basis: Delivery architecture exists; production data absent.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Official lookup coverage is sufficient after provider selection.
assumptionLedger.basis: Lookup architecture exists; coverage data absent.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Compliance defects are fixable without changing the product promise.

holes: No customer interviews or revenue data.
No operator ruling on business intent.
mitigations: Run paid beta before feature expansion.
Instrument payment, delivery, bounce, spam complaint, and refund metrics.
residualRisks: Low willingness-to-pay may persist after beta.
Government recipients may block, ignore, or complain about automated letters.
Legal/compliance obligations may make the low-price model unattractive.

decision.rationale: Promising implementation, but currently a proposed research/business plan with unresolved identity, demand, compliance, and deliverability risks.
